newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Primedia Ltd has snapped up most of entertainment group Interleisure Ltd's businesses, including the Ster Kinekor cinema chain, for 1.5 billion rand in a move to establish South Africa's first integrated entertainment company.

- The initial stake of South African Airways to be sold on foreign and local markets is likely to increase to 49 percent from the 25 percent first proposed, with full privatisation still on the cards, said Transport Minister Mac Maharaj.
- Policemen suspected by the Richmond community of being involved in political violence in the area would be redeployed, said Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufuamadi.

- Mpumalanga Premier Mathews Phosa instructed his lawyers on Tuesday to institute legal action against a woman who told the truth commission that he had intimidated her to prevent her from implicating senior Umkhonto we Sizwe (MK) members in her rape.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Primedia, the media and communications group, has paid 1.5 billion rand for virtually all the operations of Interleisure, the entertainment group which owns 300 Ster Kinekor cinemas, William Kirsh, Primedia's chief executive, said on Tuesday.

- JCI Ltd, the country's first black-owned mining house, on Tuesday posted a slide in profit at its gold division in the quarter to June 30 as production fell at its Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co and Western Areas Gold Mining Co divisions.
- The Competition Board may investigate the proposed merger of Telkom's directory operations with those of Maister Directories, Pierre Brooks, the chairman of the board, said on Tuesday.

- Strong export growth and slowing imports led the upsurge of the surplus on the trade account to a record high of 4.1 billion rand last month from 1.8 billion rand in May, Daan Colesky, commissioner for customs and excise, said on Tuesday.

- A 300 million rand investment in South Africa's first floating hotel in Durban's harbour is likely to sink without a trace because of bureaucratic bungling, said Don Robinson, chief executive of the international Robinson Hotel Group.
SAKE BEELD
- South Africa's economy was boosted on Tuesday with a positive inflation figure and trade data, but a fly in the salve was the worse than expected private sector credit figures.
- Interleisure and Primedia clinch a giant transaction.
- The taxpayer is paying over 1.33 billion rand a year to fund the South African rail commuter corporation, due to the high number of fare-dodgers on city and inter-city routes.
THE STAR
- Draft legislation to put bail beyound the reach of suspects accused of serious crimes such as murder, aggravated rape involving children and car hijacking will come before the Cabinet on Wednesday.
- Armed robberies at Soweto businesses continue with near impunity amid confusion over who -- the Government or business leaders -- should kickstart security plans put forward at a meeting last year.
- A blustering wind storm ruined the South African National Antarctic Expedition team's chances of watching the sun rise on Monday for the first time in 2-1/2 months.
